items.title: Dalton Richards Interview, 1961-03-16
items.q: I mean I've heard about him and Joe has told me plenty about it.

ctx.x: He taught himself. He really taught himself. He had old man, at first it was old man, Robichaux helped him some, then old man Humphreys, Pierron helped him out a lot. And like Joe Robichaux, Joe Robichaux was a good piano player, but he wasn't too good a musician. He was like, I wasn't what you would call a first class musician, which you don't find too many nowadays that you know, the minute they hit.
When you said old man Robichaux did you mean John Robichaux, the old violin player?

The old violin player. He used to play at the Lyric Theater when I heard it. I couldn't even go there. I was a kid then, around 18, 19, 20. I mean I've heard about him and Joe has told me plenty about it. But he has helped Joe a lot too. But still, Joe has stayed within that same track. He hasn't moved. I doubted Joe is a better piano player now than he was in 1925. See, because he never would try to improve himself. But he was a good piano player.
